conflicts: Weight: the Baby Lock spec sheet says 16 lb and a non-maker Amazon listing snippet gave 7.8 kg (17.2 lb); 16 lb is used and it is unconfirmed whether either figure is a shipping weight.

Stitch width: the Baby Lock spec sheet gives one dial range of 1.5 to 7.5 mm, while our earlier spec from a non-maker listing split it into 5.5 to 7.5 mm (4 thread) and 3.0 to 7.5 mm (3 thread); the maker range is used and the thread-count split is unverified until the manual is read.

Differential feed: the Baby Lock spec sheet gives 2:1 for gathering and 3:4 (0.75) for stretching, while our earlier spec from a non-maker listing said 0.6 to 2.0; the 0.6 lower bound is not on the spec sheet, so maker wording is used.
Threads: the spec sheet lists 2 thread stitches (rolled hem and flatlock with 2 or 3 threads), which our earlier spec and FAQ omitted; coverstitch is not listed on the spec sheet.

Model revisions: the spec sheet is for the BLE1AT-2; the original BLE1AT is an older version, and PatternReview and Reddit sources mix BLE1AT, BLE1AT-2 and the Imagine Wave (BLE3ATW), so owner evidence below is not all BLE1AT-2.
Dimensions: the 13.4 x 11 x 11.4 in figure is from a non-maker listing; the Baby Lock spec sheet does not publish dimensions.

Price: Baby Lock publishes no price and no current new dealer price was found; owners on PatternReview reported paying $950 and $1,800 new in earlier years and one Reddit comment put the Imagine near $2,000, so the catalog shows [verify].

ownerThemes.theme: PatternReview owners recommend the Imagine for running smoothly and quietly, threading easily and never needing tension adjustment thanks to the automatic thread delivery; one owner's 1998 unit was still in daily use.

One owner reports the tiny springs in the automatic tension system wore out after about two and a half years and the repair was not cheap; another disliked fiddly threading and vibration on a 2008 unit.

A PatternReview discussion thread finds the Imagine louder than a Bernina serger but praises the absence of tension and thread breakage problems; buyers asking about the BLE1AT vs BLE1AT-2 difference get told the revisions are minor.

A service technician advised one owner to pull threads through by hand after trouble with the air threader; a thread on stitches showing at the seam points to needle and differential settings rather than the machine.

editorial.verdict: A Baby Lock 4/3/2 thread serger that one dealer lists as discontinued; Jet-Air threading and Automatic Thread Delivery are maker claims that owners mostly, not always, bear out.
editorial.whoFor: A sewist who wants air threading and no tension dials, is buying used or from a dealer's remaining stock, and can live without a published coverstitch.
editorial.skipIf: You want a current model with a fresh warranty, need coverstitch, or can buy a new air-threading Juki online instead.
editorial.keySpec: 4/3/2 thread · 1,500 spm · 1.5 to 7.5 mm width · 2:1 and 3:4 differential · 16 lb
strengths: The maker lists 4, 3 and 2 thread serging with rolled hem and flatlock, so it covers more than the 3/4 thread machines it is often grouped with
Owners report threading as easy and the machine as reliable, with some units still in use after six years or more, though the evidence mixes BLE1AT, BLE1AT-2 and older units

weaknesses: Discontinued: Baby Lock lists the Imagine under previous models, and a PatternReview thread says the Victory replaced it

faqs.q: Is the Baby Lock Imagine discontinued?
faqs.a: Baby Lock lists the Imagine under previous model accessories, and a PatternReview thread on the new lineup says the Victory replaced it, though dealer pages still show Imagine listings. We found no Baby Lock statement of a discontinuation date [verify].

faqs.q: What replaced the Baby Lock Imagine?
faqs.a: A PatternReview thread says the Victory replaced it. One Reddit commenter put the Imagine near $2,000 and the Victory near $3,500; Baby Lock publishes dealer pricing only, so treat that as a belief [verify].

faqs.q: How much does a Baby Lock Imagine cost?
faqs.a: Baby Lock publishes no price for the Imagine and no current new dealer price was found, so the catalog shows [verify]. One Reddit commenter put the Imagine near $2,000, which is a belief, not a quote. Ask a dealer for a quote and ask whether the unit is new, demo or used.

faqs.q: Does the Baby Lock Imagine have tension dials?
faqs.a: Baby Lock markets Automatic Thread Delivery and no tension adjustments, which are its claims. Owner reports are mixed: one owner reports no tension issues in about six years, while others report tension trouble on stretchy fabrics and one says manual tensioning is the real annoyance.

faqs.q: How do you thread the Baby Lock Imagine, and does the air threading work?
faqs.a: Baby Lock claims Jet-Air threading of the lower loopers by lever and lists a built-in needle threader; both are maker claims. Of the owners who judged threading, most call it easy, but one buyer of a used original BLE1AT found the air threader dead, one owner had thread feed problems with taller cones that Maxi-Loc cones solved, and a service technician advised one owner to pull threads through by hand.

faqs.q: Does the Baby Lock Imagine do 2 thread stitches or coverstitch?
faqs.a: The spec sheet lists 4, 3 and 2 thread serging, with rolled hem and flatlock using 2 or 3 threads. It does not list coverstitch.

faqs.q: Is the Baby Lock Imagine the same as the Imagine Wave?
faqs.a: No. The Imagine Wave (BLE3ATW) is a separate wave stitch model, and our spec sheet covers the BLE1AT-2 only. PatternReview and Reddit posts mix BLE1AT, BLE1AT-2 and Wave units, so owner evidence here is not all BLE1AT-2.

faqs.q: Is a used Baby Lock Imagine worth buying?
faqs.a: It depends on the unit. Some owners report Imagines still running after six years or more, and one PatternReview owner reports a 1998 unit in daily use. Against that, one buyer of a used BLE1AT-1 found the air threader dead and one owner's tension springs wore out after about two and a half years with a repair that was not cheap. Confirm it is a BLE1AT-2 and ask what coverage remains on a used unit; the 25 year limited terms on the spec sheet are the maker's, not a promise for a resale.

faqs.q: What do owners say about the Baby Lock Imagine?
faqs.a: Owners mostly describe a machine that is easy to thread and reliable, with some units in use for six years or more. The repeated complaints are tension on stretchy fabrics, air threader or looper thread problems on some units, and worn tension springs on one. Our read covers 27 Reddit threads, 2 forum pages and 1 write-up from 2016 to 2026, mixing several Imagine versions, and Reddit leans toward people asking for help, so problems are over-represented.
